findings: SHA-256 seed hashes — seed.py's local hash_password() uses SHA-256 + fixed salt, so seeded demo accounts enter the DB with legacy hashes. No re-hash-on-login path exists yet; seeded accounts stay on SHA-256 until Phase 1 adds that step.

DB-outage auth bypass in middleware — get_current_user catches all non-HTTPException errors from the DB re-verification call and falls through with the token's stale claims. A DB outage means deactivated accounts remain active and stale roles persist. Consider failing closed (401 or 503) on DB errors.

Allowlist empty = all URLs permitted — REST_BASE_URL_ALLOWLIST defaults to empty in both the shim and worker, skipping the allowlist check. The .env.example also ships with the variable empty, so a production deploy copied from the example gets no allowlist enforcement. The example should ship with a placeholder or require an explicit opt-out.
